description: Step 1 of the lint. Declare what the app does (activities) and where it will operate (jurisdiction slugs), from the app's own code: ask the user which app if they have not said, and lint only one whose code you can open (the open folder, a public repository, one the user connected, or code pasted into the chat). If you cannot open it, say so and do not declare from a description. Get back the validated, canonical profile plus what the law library holds for each jurisdiction, so the depth of a run is known before it is spent. Write the returned profile into the project's lexlint.yml, or show it to the user to commit where you cannot write there, and pass it to run_lint. Stores nothing server-side. An unknown activity or a malformed slug is refused here rather than silently weakening a lint later. Costs one upstream request for any number of jurisdictions. It answers the same coverage question check_access's own jurisdictions preview does, off a request check_access spends either way, so asking both is redundant, never costlier: they just repeat the same answer. This tool needs sign-in or an UnGovr Open Data key (metered per request; get one at https://ungovr.org/cli-login?client=lexlint).

activities.description: What the app does. Allowed: crawls_web, trains_models, generates_content, deploys_chatbot, deploys_companion_chatbot, deploys_mental_health_chatbot, automated_outreach, places_automated_calls, sends_automated_texts, sends_commercial_email, sends_faxes, high_risk_decisions, processes_voice, processes_biometrics, processes_personal_data, processes_deidentified_data, publishes_adult_content, operates_social_platform, serves_minors, operates_app_store, ships_mobile_app, ships_consumer_interface, relies_on_digital_identity, collects_e_signatures, ships_encryption, serves_sanctioned_destination, aggregates_content, distributes_software_product, handles_health_records, provides_financial_services, operates_essential_service, is_listed_company, provides_telecom_services, provides_cloud_services, provides_general_purpose_ai_model, is_frontier_developer, serves_education_institutions, serves_k12_schools, serves_higher_education, statutory_requests, records_calls, records_text_chat, tracks_devices, is_bank, is_lender, is_insurer, is_securities_firm, is_payment_provider, is_crypto_asset_provider, employment_decisions, credit_decisions, insurance_decisions, housing_decisions, education_decisions, health_care_decisions, public_services_decisions, justice_decisions, generates_text, generates_images, generates_video, generates_audio

activities_left_out.description: Activities the developer was asked about and said this software does not do. Today it answers processes_personal_data: unsent, a declaration naming any activity its code settles is matched as if it processes personal data, with an info coverage line, until the developer answers. It also answers the two chatbot kinds: deploys_chatbot with neither declared nor left out is matched as if it is both, with an info coverage line. And it answers the two model-provider roles: trains_models with a role neither declared nor left out is asked about it, with an info coverage line counting the laws that bind it. Left out, serves_education_institutions says no school, college or university runs or buys this software, so serves_minors no longer brings school law in.

derived.description: true adds derived findings: the records an app holds to meet the deadlines the matched laws set, inferred by LexLint and traced to each law. false leaves them out; omitted, the server default applies.

flows.description: Where this software stores or sends personal data across a border, one entry per route: [{"from": "eu", "to": "us", "data": "personal", "basis": "contract_clauses"}]. from and to are jurisdiction slugs, as jurisdictions takes them; data is personal or sensitive; basis is the transfer mechanism the route relies on: adequacy, contract_clauses, binding_rules, certification, authority_approval, consent, derogation, unknown. [] when asked and no personal data leaves the jurisdiction it was collected in. Ask the developer; never infer it from the code. Each cross-border transfer finding then names the declared flows that leave its jurisdiction. No finding is dropped or downgraded on a flow.

jurisdictions.description: Jurisdiction slugs, lowercase, "/"-separated (e.g. "us", "us/ca", "eu", "kr"). A slug is the jurisdiction's UnGovr Atlas path: California is https://ungovr.org/us/ca and its Atlas ID is urn:ungovr:us/ca. Its ISO 3166 code, US-CA, is accepted too. A deeper or unresearched path resolves to the nearest jurisdiction with law, and the jurisdictions whose law is researched are listed at https://lexlint.io/law for the developer to check; name every jurisdiction the app operates in: one left off is unlinted, not passed.

public_sector.description: Is this software run by a public body (body), sold to or run for public bodies (supplier), both, or neither (none)? Ask the developer every time the profile is declared; never infer it from the code. Omitted, duties binding only public bodies are reported as the caller's, and run_lint counts them in a coverage line. body: A public body runs this software. supplier: You sell this software to public bodies or run it for them.

public_sector_functions.description: Which kinds of public body run or buy this software. Ask only when public_sector is body or supplier, and never infer it from the code. One or more of: general (a general-purpose public body, such as a city hall, a state department or a federal agency), law_enforcement (police and sheriffs), corrections (prisons, jails, parole and probation), prosecution_courts (courts, prosecutors and public defenders), public_education (public schools, school districts and public universities), public_health (health departments and public hospitals), elections (election offices), public_benefits (agencies deciding welfare, unemployment or Medicaid eligibility), emergency_services (911 centers, fire and emergency medical services). A duty that binds only another kind is reported as someone else's; a duty that binds every public body always reaches you. Omitted, every public-body duty reaches you, and run_lint counts the ones that bind a single kind in a coverage line.

regulated_sector.description: Whose duty a financial-law row is. Is this software run by a bank, insurer or other regulated financial entity (body), supplied to one (supplier), or neither (none)? {"financial": "supplier"}. Ask when provides_financial_services or a license class (is_bank, is_lender, is_insurer, is_securities_firm, is_payment_provider, is_crypto_asset_provider) is declared; never infer it. It routes and never matches, so a supplier still declares the classes of its customers. Omitted, the entity's duties are reported as the caller's, and run_lint counts them in a coverage line.

financial.description: body: A bank, insurer or other regulated financial entity runs this software. supplier: You supply this software to a bank, insurer or other regulated financial entity.

roles.description: Which role this software's maker holds under each regime, keyed by axis: ai_system (provider, deployer, importer, distributor, product_manufacturer, authorised_representative, the EU AI Act's operators) and personal_data (controller, processor, the GDPR's). {"ai_system": ["provider"], "personal_data": ["processor"]}; "none" alone when asked and none applies. Ask the developer; never infer it from the code. Omitted, an axis routes nothing and run_lint counts the duties a role would move in a coverage line.

ai_system.description: provider: You develop an AI system or general-purpose AI model, or have one developed, and put it on the EU market or into service under your own name or trademark, paid or free. deployer: You use an AI system under your own authority, other than in a personal, non-professional activity. importer: You are located or established in the EU and place on its market an AI system bearing the name or trademark of someone established outside it. distributor: You make an AI system available on the EU market as part of its supply chain, without being its provider or importer. product_manufacturer: You put a product on the EU market under your own name with an AI system inside it as a safety component, which makes you that system's provider. authorised_representative: You are located or established in the EU and hold a written mandate from a provider outside it to carry out its obligations under the Act on its behalf.

personal_data.description: controller: You decide, alone or jointly with others, why and how personal data is processed. processor: You process personal data on behalf of a controller.
